# @jpisgeek/dashboard-report-view

Turns an explicit snapshot into a human-readable HTML report with local text and
state filters, observation time, evidence, and a refresh button. A host handler
factory embeds it into an existing server without starting a new listener. The
host authorizes every read and refresh, then runs one configured Swamp workflow.
A portable successor to a working fleet health and leaderboard report prototype;
it does not install a native Swamp dashboard page.

**Version** `2026.11.08.1` · **License** MIT · **Source**
https://github.com/jpisgeek/slog-bog/tree/main/dashboard-report-view

## Install

```
swamp extension pull @jpisgeek/dashboard-report-view
```

## `@jpisgeek/dashboard-report-view`

### Arguments

| argument                              | type                                             | required | default | description |
| ------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ | -------- | ------- | ----------- |
| `snapshot`                            | object                                           | yes      |         |             |
| `snapshot.schemaVersion`              | number                                           | yes      |         |             |
| `snapshot.title`                      | string                                           | yes      |         |             |
| `snapshot.observedAt`                 | string                                           | yes      |         |             |
| `snapshot.sections`                   | array of object                                  | yes      |         |             |
| `snapshot.sections[].title`           | string                                           | yes      |         |             |
| `snapshot.sections[].rows`            | array of object                                  | yes      |         |             |
| `snapshot.sections[].rows[].label`    | string                                           | yes      |         |             |
| `snapshot.sections[].rows[].value`    | string \| number \| null                         | yes      |         |             |
| `snapshot.sections[].rows[].state`    | `healthy` \| `attention` \| `unknown` \| `stale` | yes      |         |             |
| `snapshot.sections[].rows[].evidence` | string                                           | no       |         |             |

### Methods

#### `render`

Render explicit state into a filterable HTML report and retain its canonical
snapshot.

No arguments.

### Data written

| resource   | lifetime | fields                                             | description             |
| ---------- | -------- | -------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------- |
| `snapshot` | 30d      | `schemaVersion`, `title`, `observedAt`, `sections` | Canonical report state. |

## Example

```yaml
globalArguments:
  snapshot:
    schemaVersion: 1
    title: Fleet health
    observedAt: "2026-11-08T12:00:00.000Z"
    sections:
      - title: mac-mini
        rows:
          - label: Disk space
            value: null
            state: unknown
            evidence: No observation yet
      - title: mac-studio
        rows:
          - label: Memory
            value: null
            state: stale
            evidence: Awaiting a fresh Swamp check
```

## Caveats

See USE-CASES.md for the Swamp Quest flow, fleet monitoring and other
compositions, and PROPOSAL.md for the native dashboard integration request. The
renderer reads only supplied data and never fetches scores, infers freshness, or
starts schedules. Producers must label stale and unavailable state explicitly.
Offline HTML supports filters; live refresh requires the existing host adapter
described in HOSTING.md.

## Security

No secrets, machine addresses, provider access, shell, process, or listener. All
snapshot strings are HTML-escaped. The host must authenticate and authorize
every request with scoped Swamp grants. Refresh is an empty POST to one fixed
path, with same-origin checks and a custom header. Request data never chooses a
workflow or supplies inputs. Errors suppress internal details. Hosting HTML as a
privileged dashboard document requires an appropriate isolation policy; native
dashboard embedding remains an upstream proposal.

See [SECURITY.md](https://github.com/jpisgeek/slog-bog/blob/main/SECURITY.md)
for the release gates every version passes before it reaches the registry.
